text:
tobias: FYI seeing a reproducible bump in p99 memory after the AWQ->FP8 KV dtype change. Host: ded-dev-03, model: rw-gpt-awq-7b, seq=2048, b=6. +22-28% reserved mem across runs.

priya: ugh, timing? did this land on main or a release branch?

tobias: landed on main yesterday (commit 9f3b2c), perf CI didn't catch it because unit batches were smaller. repro script attached below.

priya: paste the quick `torch.cuda.memory_reserved()` snapshot?

tobias: ```
# running warmup + single infer
Allocated: 9.1 GB
Reserved: 11.8 GB
Cache: 2.2 GB
After second step:
Allocated: 10.5 GB
Reserved: 14.4 GB
```

eve: looks like KV cache path is doing an upcast to fp32 somewhere — AWQ should keep ahead with fp16/uint8-backed buffers. Did the dtype detection fall back?

tobias: from quick grepping the diff i see `kv_cache_upcast=True` gated by `model.dtype==torch.float16` check; AWQ path sets dtype=fp8 but downstream checks don't cover fp8, so code hits the generic upcast.

kai: that matches. We added an implicit upcast in `kernel_select.py` to avoid numeric drift with older kernels; it uses `if not is_fp16_like(model.dtype): do_upcast()` and fp8 isn't considered fp16-like.

priya: two angles: (1) make fp8 be recognized as fp16-like for KV path (safer), (2) make an explicit AWQ fast-path that keeps kv buffers quantized and only upcasts when necessary. Which is lower risk?

eve: lower risk = 1) minimal patch: treat fp8/awq dtypes as fp16-like for allocator/kv decisions. But risk = might hide real numeric issues in kernels that require float32.

kai: perf-wise 1) is best immediate fix. 2) is better long-term — introduce `kv_upcast_policy` with options: `always`, `on-demand`, `never` and have a canary rollout.

perf-bot: perf/regressions#782 opened (automated triage) linking the commit, test vectors, and `nvidia-smi` traces.

tobias: repro script: ```bash
# run in ded-dev-03
python infra/tools/run_infer.py 
  --model rw-gpt-awq-7b 
  --seq_len 2048 
  --batch 6 
  --profile gpu > /tmp/awq_kv_profile.log
```
log excerpt:```
2026-03-17 11:02:12 [profile] kernel_select: chosen kernel=matmul_fp16_fused (fallback=true)
2026-03-17 11:02:12 [profile] kv_cache: buffer_dtype=float32 (source=upcast_path)
```

priya: can someone bisect to the exact line change? I can ship a hotfix if it's a single gating addition.

kai: already looked — change in kernel_select PR 9f3b2c added `fallback_upcast=True` and forgot to extend `fp16_like = {torch.float16}` set. PR is tiny. I can push a targeted branch to treat AWQ dtypes as fp16_like.

eve: before we revert or patch, we should run a small-scale throughput test to ensure no perf regression for older rtx nodes. I'd add a quick ci job: `ci/perf/kv_dtype_smoke` that runs batch sizes 1/4/8 and reports reserved/resident deltas.

tobias: good call. I'll run smoke on ded-dev-01/02/03 and paste results by EOD.

perf-bot: perf/regressions#782 updated with ded-dev-01 results (reserve delta +24%).

priya: action items:
- kai: push `fp8 -> fp16_like` guard branch + run smoke (ETA 2h)
- eve: add ci/perf smoke job (ETA today)
- tobias: run ded-dev smoke and attach logs (ETA EOD)
- if green: ship hotfix patch with canary rollout (no rollback plan needed)

kai: starting branch `fix/kv-fp8-pixel` now. will tag for canary in console.

tobias: note for postmortem: we should add unit tests that exercise `kv_cache` dtype decisions across {fp16,fp8,awq,float32}. Lack of coverage is why ci missed this.

eve: agreed. also include a perf-harness scenario with seq_len 2048 and batch 6-8 in future perf matrix.

priya: thx all — ping me on thread when the canary is up so I can run regression checks. :thumbsup:

kai: pushed branch, smoke results attached in PR comments. initial numbers look back to baseline on dev nodes. will start canary deploy in 30m.

perf-bot: canary deploy started for branch `fix/kv-fp8-pixel` on ded-dedicated-pprod-1

tobias: thanks — will monitor memory graphs and alert on >10% delta.

priya: moving this to short postmortem after canary is healthy.
